newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - April 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - April 8.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY

- Police Commissioner George Fivaz was seen by the government as "ineffective" and clashes with policing minister Sydney Mufamadi were intended to "push him out" of the police service, a senior government source said.

- Several recent high-level resignations and a high debt burden have sparked concern within the government about the long-term future of the loss-making South African Housing Trust, which was set up to faciliate home loans to the poor.

- The African National Congress expelled KwaZulu-Natal member of parliament Sifiso Nkabinde from the party, alleging that he had been an informer for the apartheid government who was "still reporting to his handlers".

- Oil and fuels group Engen lifted net income 36.4 percent to 191 million rand in the six months to February after strong local demand and improved inventory profits helped offset flat refining margins and operational problems.

- An oversight by three broking firms involving Servgro International's partial unbundling resulted in their purchase of 20,600 shares at 23 rand each, which the market later valued as low as seven rand per share.
BUSINESS REPORT
- The government was committed to selling its entire stake in South African Airways SAA.CN over time, Public Enterprises Minister Stella Sigcau said.
- Sun International South Africa confirmed it had acquired a Midrand property site earmarked for the largest casino project in the area.
- The long, hard climb to profitability for Engen took a leap forward with the announcement of stronger-than-expected earnings growth in the first half.
- Pepkor has started to flex its muscles at Waltons Stationery Co Ltd, which is not expected to improve its poor interim results in the full year to February 28.
SAKE-BEELD

- Economic indicators for this year are looking better, with a consensus forecast by economists of gross domestic product growth of 2.35 percent, slightly up from February's prediction of 2.21 percent.

- Around 78,000 working days were lost in the first quarter of this year through strikes, compared to the 175,000 lost during the corresponding period of last year, according to labour researchers Andrew Levy and Associates.
- Engen increased its earnings in the six months to end-February by 21.6 percent to 107 cents per share.
THE STAR
- ANC KwaZulu-Natal Midlands leader Sifiso Nkabinde was expelled from the party with immediate effect on charges of being a spy and agent provocateur.
- National police commissioner George Fivaz confirmed he would not be resigning after a war of words with policing minister Sydney Mufamadi.

- The state South African Broadcasting Corp's 16 radio stations shed almost five million listeners -- a sixth of their total audience -- in the second half of last year and new figures due later this month will most likely bring more bad news.
